utterances.text: The Chamber has received evidence that the overwhelming majority of the civilians at the Vlahovic school were Muslims. Is that also something you learned later?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO RAJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we'll take a break. And we'd like to see you back in 20 minutes from now. You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll take a break, and we'll resume at quarter past 12.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the witness be escorted in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Could we have 65 ter 31332.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: While it comes up, sir, you mention in your statement that Rasadnik prisoners were exchanged in Sarajevo. Now, your commander, Mr. Kusic, would approve at least some of those exchanges; right?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO RAJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And here, we see a document emanating --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There seems to be something ...

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Let me try again briefly. It seems the problem has been solved.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: We see a document emanating from the 1st Podrinje Brigade command dated the 29th of May, 1993. This is an example of one such exchange that Mr. Kusic is approving; right?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO RAJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And is it your understanding that the purported reception centre for Muslim residents in Rogatica mentioned in the document, is it your understanding that that refers to Rasadnik?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO RAJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I tender this document, 65 ter 31332.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be Exhibit P6854, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, I want to turn to the corrections to paragraph 10. In your initial signed statement, you said: "The Crisis Staff was formed at the end of May, beginning of June, after the negotiations with the Muslims who had actual power failed. Vlahovic and Rasadnik were outside its purview and under the control of the Rogatica Brigade." Now, your evidence Thursday was that Vlahovic school was created by the civilian authorities and Rasadnik was partially under the control of the TO and military and partially under the control of the police; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO RAJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: When you say the civilian authorities were responsible for the Vlahovic school, which civilian authorities do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO RAJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: The police.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, you say now that you don't know anything about the competencies, composition or work of the Crisis Staff. The Chamber has received evidence that, in fact, it was formed well before the end of May. And that's, for instance, P3913 [Realtime transcript read in error "P3193"]. You don't know when it was formed either; right?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO RAJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know. The information was not that accessible to us for the reasons I already mentioned. We were quite far from that part of the town.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: How is it that you know that the civilian police, you now say, were responsible for the Vlahovic school?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO RAJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Later, after 1993 when I was there, I learnt about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, could I ask you one question in between. You responded to a question put to you by Mr. Traldi that you do not know when the Crisis Staff was formed. Nevertheless, in your statement, it reads: "The Crisis Staff was formed at the end of May, beginning of June ..." Now, how can you say that if you tell us today that you do not know when it was formed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The information arrived with some delay. So we did not know exactly when it was formed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But in your statement, you say it was formed end of May, beginning of June. Whereas you now again confirm that you do not know. What makes you say it was formed then and now to say: "Well, I don't know"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I thought that, based on subsequent information, we did not have the precise date of its formation. But we did know that it had been set up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: How did you then know that it was the end of May, beginning of June?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Information came, and I repeat, we were far away. We did not know about the events immediately. But that was more or less when I learnt, that's when I learnt.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you say "information came," it's -- what information?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] About the formation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But what then exactly did you learn about it? Who did it, where was it done? Why late May, early June? Why not early May? What was it? Or if you just don't know, if you say, "We just heard that it was formed," then tell us as well, or give us the precise detailed information you received.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I only heard that it had been set up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: From whom did you hear that? If you remember.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] From my superior commander, who was up there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And who was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Dragomir Paunovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I have follow-up questions. When did you get this information, that it had been formed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In late May. I'm not 100 per cent sure. More or less about that time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Late May of which year?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: So you signed this statement on the 6th of June, 2014.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You had this information from Mr. Paunovic already.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This information refers to the year 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes. But you gave this information in your statement on the 6th of June, 2014; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And so when you made this statement, you knew that, according to Dragomir Paunovic, this had been formed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. But I spoke based on the information that I had at the time, the contemporaneous information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And as you sit here today, you testified that you don't know when it was formed, or whether it was formed, which is what Judge Orie was asking you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I've just told you that I learnt only subsequently.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I understand that. But all this you were asked before you testified today, and today you have given two versions.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I stand by my statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Which one? That you don't know or that Paunovic told you it was formed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That he told me that the Crisis Staff had been formed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: So when you said you don't know, you were not correct.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know the exact date.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm not asking you about the date. When you said you didn't know when it was formed, you were not correct.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe that the information that I've shared with you is accurate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You are not answering my question. Okay. I leave it at that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I apologise. If you can direct us, Your Honour, when this witness said today that Crisis Staff was not formed. I don't remember that portion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Isn't this what Judge Orie was asking him just now? If you look at page 51, line 12, Judge Orie says: "Witness, could I ask you one question in between." I think he meant one question. "You responded to a question put to you by Mr. Traldi that you do not know when the Crisis Staff was formed. Nevertheless, in your statement it reads: 'The Crisis Staff was formed in the -- at the end of May, beginning of June ...'"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And the critical --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] -- is when --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: The critical question was on line 6 [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Not about the formation, only the date.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Line 6. Mr. Traldi asked on line 4 and 5 of page 51: "You don't know when it was formed either; right?" The answer was: "No, I don't know. The information was not that accessible ..."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There may be some issue about the when or the whether. Let's carefully look at that. And that is, I take it, Mr. Lukic, that you wanted to draw our attention to and that is well understood.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Just on the same line -- line 4, rather, of page 51, Mr. President, I've been recorded - perhaps I misspoke - as referring to P3193, and should have referred to P3913.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's hereby corrected. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, as to control over Rasadnik, the Chamber has received evidence that beginning in late 1992, the commander there was a man named Vinko Bojic, also known as Vili, and that he was a member of the Rogatica Brigade. That is correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO RAJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Personally I didn't know the man. However, I do believe that he was a member of the Rogatica Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, the Chamber has also received evidence that Mr. Kusic reported a number of times to the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps command - P312, P459, P6803, for instance - on people being moved into the premises of the secondary school. Were you aware that he was doing so?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO RAJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: When you made corrections to your statement regarding who had control over the Vlahovic school and over Rasadnik, were you aware that General Mladic was charged with crimes there?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO RAJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And could the Prosecution please have P6804.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, sir, I'd asked earlier if you agreed with me that civilians were held in the Rasadnik camp. Now this is a document dated the 1st of February, 1993, and it's being forwarded by the Drina Corps command to the 4th Podrinje Light Infantry Brigade. It's referring to prisoners of war in the Vili camp, Rogatica. Now to confirm again, Vili was the name -- the nickname of the Rasadnik camp commander, Vinko Bojic; right?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO RAJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I heard. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'd ask that you just look at this list for a moment, focussing on the names and the years of birth, roughly 1 through 15 or so. Can you confirm orally by saying "yes" once you've had an opportunity to review that information.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO RAJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: None of the names rings any bells.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Based on your experience in Rogatica municipality, these are Muslim names; right?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO RAJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And at number 4, we see Hanua Kustura. That's a woman's name; right?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO RAJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: We see that she was born in 1892.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO RAJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Earlier, in reference to Rasadnik, you said it was soldiers and prisoners of war held there. So my question is: Were you aware that the prisoners of war held at Rasadnik included 100-year-old women?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO RAJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not aware of that. I am certain of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, that completes my examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Traldi. Any further questions, Mr. Lukic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just a few one -- but I don't think that I understood well the last line of questions regarding villa so I might clarify it with the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] First of all, good afternoon yet again.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO RAJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is the villa one and the same as Rasadnik, do you know that? Is there any other villa? Are we talking about one and the same building? I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO RAJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, the two are not the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So what is the villa?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO RAJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: The villa is a catering facility.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: How far is it from Rasadnik; do you know?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO RAJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the Rogatica municipality, there was just one, and it was some 15 kilometres away.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. This puts the villa away then. And now just let's go back to today's record. Page 44, line 10.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we do so --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- Mr. Lukic, you are talking about the villa. Now I see in the original Vili between quotation marks. And --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yeah. It's grammar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But the quotation marks stand for what?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I would say villa. We change our words even under the quotation marks. There are different extensions. And if you want --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Let's then ask the witness -- Are aware of any persons being detained in a villa where you said there was a catering facility?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you know anything at all about civilians being detained anywhere in Rogatica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: During that period of time, i.e., January and February 1993, did you move around the area where the villa was located?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO RAJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know what was in the villa on the 1st February 1993? Was it a restaurant or not?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO RAJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: It had been a restaurant, but by then, it was empty and abandoned.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Before that, I was going to ask you something that was recorded on page 44, line 10 earlier today. My learned friend asked you, and I'm going to read the question and answer in English and you will receive proper interpretation. And then I'll have a question for you. I quote: [In English] "I have two questions for -- about this. First, was it common in the Rogatica Brigade to refer to non-Serbs as Ustashas? "A. Well, yes." [Interpretation] The question, therefore, is this: Were all Muslims and Croats referred to as Ustashas or fighters or juniors or seniors or older people or younger people? Who was referred to as Ustasha?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO RAJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those who had been known from the Second World War, those who were the organiser of the events that took place in 1944.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us look at P3942.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is there a new subject, or are we still on the Ustasha issue?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The same issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then I'll wait for a second.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: "The unit from Borik, at the invitation of the Serbian people from Visegrad, took part in the rescuing of the Serbian people by engaging against the already established Ustasha formations." That was read out to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Sorry, that's not the same document. I don't know what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I think if I might assist.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's P3924.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic did not require my assistance, it turned out, as usual.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, anyways. I'm sorry, and we need page 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is an analysis of combat readiness. It was drafted on the 25th of February, 1993. When -- where -- and in that document, the already established Ustasha formations are mentioned. Who is that a reference to?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO RAJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Muslim forces. The Green Berets.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The Prosecutor skipped something and I'd like to see it. It says here, and I'm going to read the entire sentence: "At the same time, the somewhat well-organised Serbian units, based on the TO principle, carried out training in order to prevent sabotage activities which had already taken place against the Serbian people in Bosnia." Do you know whether there had been any attacks and sabotage activities against the Serbian villages there in the months of March and April 1992?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO RAJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first casualties were recorded on the 6th of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. Do you know anything about this group of 40 Serbian lads who were SDS activists? They had volunteered to attend courses on anti-sabotage activities.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO RAJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was never in touch with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know what kind of training took place in Han Pijesak, Pazarici and --

utterances.speaker: MILENKO RAJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. At the time, were you able to follow any Muslim media; and do you know what they called the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO RAJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: They called us Chetniks.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you consider yourself to be a Chetnik?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO RAJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you consider that to be praise or an insult?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO RAJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: So we were Serb soldiers, soldiers of the Army of Republika Srpska. That is to say, that is our name, and then we considered Chetniks to be an insult.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Rajak. That is all we had for you.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO RAJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you, too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lukic. Mr. Rajak, I have one or two questions. You were asked whether, during January and February 1993, whether you moved around in the area where the villa was located. Your answer was: "No, I did not." And then you were asked: "Do you know what was in the villa on the 1st of February 1993? Was there -- was it a restaurant or not?" And then you said: "It had been a restaurant, but by then, it was empty and abandoned." How did you know that it was empty and abandoned when you never moved around in that period of time in the area where the villa was located?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I didn't move around but because of the geographical position that it was in, I know that there was no one there. Or we assumed that there was no one there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Because we have seen a document which suggests that there were a lot of people detained there, including elderly women. So I'm just wondering why -- or how you can be so certain about the place being abandoned. Or is it that you say: Well, it was just my assumption that the place was abandoned and I do not know for sure.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, the only one that was up there in the municipality of Rogatica, I know that it had been abandoned. If we're talking about the same thing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, of course, I do not know. But, again, a minute ago, you said: It was just my assumption that there was no one there. And now you say: I know that it had been abandoned. But do you know whether anyone would have moved in again late January, early February 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, no one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And you consider this document which says there are many people detained there to be a fraud or ... what makes you so sure if you have not been there to say no one moved in, whereas there is a document, an official document, which gives a long list of people detained there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Explanation. Rasadnik is something different from villa. Villa is totally different. It's not the same facility.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think the questions that were put to you about the villa, whether there was a restaurant, whether it had been abandoned, the document which was shown to you was interpreted as dealing with the villa as well. I asked about that, whether Vili would mean villa. Yes, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Not by us, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, no, I'm not -- no. I know that. That's -- but that was ... so, still, the question is: You followed more or less the suggestion that the Vili camp was the villa. And you said there was a catering facility. It had been abandoned. And there was no one there, although you have never been there. I'm slightly confused by that evidence. Unless you say: What was presented to me as the Vili camp could not be the villa I talked about.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a villa that was abandoned. As far as I understood the Prosecutor, this is the nickname of a particular gentleman, Vili is his nickname. It is not the facility called villa.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So your answers about what you know as the villa has got nothing to do with what you saw on this document which is about the Vili camp and which, indeed, was interpreted by the Prosecution in quite a different way from how the Defence interpreted it. But ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The villa facility has nothing whatsoever to do with this other thing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that other thing referred to in the document as the Vili camp, does that ring a bell what that could be?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's not Logor Vili. It is Rasadnik. But, actually, the name Vinko Bojic, his nickname is Vili.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So Logor Vili, for you, is a reference to Rasadnik.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. I have no further questions. Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: It appears to me that Mr. Lukic might have some arising out of the Chamber's and to preserve the order, I might defer to him, if that suits.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that is the preferred order.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I would just then ask for P6804 to be brought on our screens.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We're not going to invite the witness to interpret documents as you know, Mr. -- it's for the Chamber and for the parties to do that --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I would just ask him to carefully read the first sentence of the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm quite willing to read it carefully. But we're not going to ask the witness, a document which is unknown to him, to interpret that. You may put questions about the document; that's fine. But we're not seeking the witness to do the job of the Chamber and the parties.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Rajak, I'm going to reading something out, the first sentence from the document that is before you on the screen. So it is a document of the Drina Corps command. It was sent to the command of the 4th PLPBR to PP Cerovic, and this is how the sentence reads: "Pursuant to your request, we hereby submit the list of prisoners of war at the Vili camp, Rogatica." So it is the Vili camp, Logor Vili. Have you heard of a camp in Rogatica called Vili or villa?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO RAJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I haven't heard. Only Rasadnik. And Mr. Bojic's nickname is Vili.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is a military document. Did you have an opportunity to see documents of the Drina Corps command frequently?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO RAJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Was it customary in our part of the world for facilities and POW camps to be named by people's nicknames or after person's nicknames?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO RAJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not have an opportunity to see something like that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: May I ask one question for clarification. What was Mr. Bojic's position in February 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that he was a guard over there at Rasadnik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: A guard of what?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of Rasadnik. The Rasadnik facility.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: What is the Rasadnik facility exactly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Where military prisoners were and soldiers of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And he was a guard there, in your opinion and your recollection. Was he the only guard or were there more guards, or did he have a specific duty?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know. I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I shall conclude by putting this question. When answering Judge Fluegge's question, you said that military prisoners were there and soldiers of Republika Srpska. When you say "soldiers of Republika Srpska," in what status were they?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO RAJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Soldiers who did not carry out the military tasks that they were given, so they were drunk, they abandoned the front line, and things like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So they were arrested and detained?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO RAJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, detained.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Except for these detainees, lest there be any confusion, were there other Serb soldiers there who were not detained and who were guarding all of these people?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO RAJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lukic. Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Just briefly, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: As of the 1st of February, 1993, you were a member of the military police in the Rogatica Brigade; right?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO RAJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: The villa and the Rasadnik camp are both within the area of responsibility of the Rogatica Brigade; right?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO RAJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: One of the things that military police have as part of their responsibility is prisoners of war, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO RAJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And just to confirm, you were not aware of any prisoners of war ever being held in a building called the villa; right?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO RAJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: That's all, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Traldi. Mr. Rajak, this concludes your testimony. On behalf of the Chamber, I'd like to thank you very much for coming to The Hague and for having answered all the questions, and for having had the patience this morning to come later. And I'd also like to thank you for having answered all the questions that were put to you by the parties and by this Bench, and I wish you a safe return home again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, I'm looking at the clock and I'm wondering what would be best. Perhaps to take the break now and not to start the testimony of the next witness for just ten or 15 minutes, but, rather, to take the break now and then to --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Go till the end of the day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I don't know how much time you have reserved for that witness, but ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I asked for an extension of time. Since we have additional documents, I will not go anything through his statement, just I would go in connection with his statement through some documents since we have a lot of non-associated exhibits.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is there any problem as far as notice is concerned in this respect. Because if you say: I'm going to ask the witness not about his statement but about other matters, that may --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It is in connection with his statement, of course, but it's not the documents from the statement but the documents marked as non-associated exhibits.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. Last night, Mr. Lukic informed us that he had four more documents and wanted to change the estimate from 30 minutes to two hours, and we heard a little bit more information about this witness. And the Prosecution is not objecting to that, though we'd obviously prefer that not happen, and I would ask that my estimate from two hours go up to three hours. I hope I don't have to use that but given the late notice and I'm really not sure where Mr. Lukic is going on this -- but we do know this witness, he's testified many times, and we're ready to go.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, Mr. Lukic, that is one and a half hour from for four documents, I understand. That's 22 and a half minutes a document which is not --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I wish it's only four documents. As Mr. McCloskey said, I informed them about four new documents that are not on the list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, you know --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I make two observations. The first is that the last time you asked for more time, that the way in which your examination-in-chief developed was such that we thought that you should stay within your original time-limits and you even stayed within it more than expected, so that was moving in various directions rather quickly. That's one. Second, it seems there is a tendency for the Defence to --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's only me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's only you. You take the full blame for it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Nevertheless it will have consequences for the total amount of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We'll stick with our allocated amount of time, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which means that you would have to skip witnesses at a certain stage or make them 92 bis or -- well, there are various options but --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. If you would give that thorough thought, then -- and you say you want to conclude today, that's -- well, that's not within two hours, but -- we'll take a break, and we'll resume at 1.30, and we'll closely monitor and follow the way in which the examination-in-chief develops.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We're waiting for the witness to be escorted into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Kralj. Before you give evidence, the Rules require that you make a solemn declaration. The text is now handed out to you. I'd like to invite you to make that solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please be seated, Mr. Kralj. Mr. Kralj, you'll first be examined by Mr. Lukic. You find him to your left. Mr. Lukic is counsel for Mr. Mladic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day, Mr. Kralj.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KRALJ
utterances.text: Good day.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: For the record, could you please state your name and surname, slowly.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KRALJ
utterances.text: I am Slavko Kralj.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kralj, did you give a statement to the representatives of General Mladic's Defence?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KRALJ
utterances.text: I gave a statement to the representatives of General Mladic's Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have document 1D1644 in e-court, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You see the document on the screen before you now. Do you see a signature on this page?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KRALJ
utterances.text: I see the document, and I see the signature on this page in the Serbian version.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you recognise the signature?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KRALJ
utterances.text: That is my signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us now take a look at the last page, please, the last page of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Again, on this page, in the B/C/S version, can you recognise the signature?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KRALJ
utterances.text: Yes, that is my signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kralj, the information that you provided in this written statement, are they correct and truthful?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KRALJ
utterances.text: All the information I provided in this statement is correct and truthful, and I wouldn't change any of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Would you give the same answers if the same questions were put to you today?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KRALJ
utterances.text: If I were to be asked the same questions, I would give the same answers.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I would like to tender Mr. Kralj's statement along with the associated exhibits.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, first, the statement would -- Mr. Registrar, would receive number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D712, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D712 is admitted into evidence. Mr. Lukic, we leave the associated exhibits, which are quite high in number, for a while, because we would like to think about the number --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: There are eight.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me just have a look.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Three already have P numbers and eight associated exhibits are left for admission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We'll deal with them separately, but I do agree with that you it's not -- it's not that high a number that -- to have great concerns about. Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I will read the statement summary of Mr. Kralj, and then, as I informed Your Honours, I will have questions for this witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- in regard of some additional documents we didn't tender as associated exhibits.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Slavko Kralj was lieutenant-colonel in VRS and liaison officer with UNPROFOR during relevant period. Until autumn 1994, witness was in 1st Krajina Corps, and since then, he was in VRS Main Staff Department for Relation with UNPROFOR. Witness will testify that the 1st Krajina Corps received information from VRS Main Staff on routes of UNPROFOR convoys and their passage through check-points, which information was further sent to subordinate units in order to facilitate uninterrupted passage of those convoys. He will testify on often abuse of these convoys, on fuel smuggling, as well as of surveillance equipment. Witness was directly subordinated to Djurdjic Milos, who was chief of -- chief of his department and that his main task was to translate notifications received from UNPROFOR, which mostly were requests for passage of convoys.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, this summary is so wrong that I have to object at this point. He's never testified that his main task was mere translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's not mere translation, main task. He had other --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: His main tasks. Yeah. That's not what he's testified to. I've heard him testify many times. And he also had responsibility not for just UNPROFOR convoys --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: -- which you've so far only said. So this is beginning to mislead the public and the Court, if --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, please be very cautious there. You may remember that it was only last week that I had to remind that you parts of your summary did not reflect anything that was in the statement. So if you want to postpone your summary any further so as to verify whether it is an accurate summary of the statement, you have an opportunity to do so. If you'd continue, then I expect you to be very precise. And, again, it's in order to inform the public. Therefore, you can make up your mind --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: First of all, the summary is not too long. I think we have the rule, how long the summary can be, and it doesn't -- hasn't reached that limit yet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, it is not about length. It is about accuracy.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That -- the first objection was it was too lengthy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I haven't heard that, as a matter of fact. You -- that is a wrong summary of what Mr. McCloskey told us. Perhaps "so wrong" you understood as "so long."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Oh, maybe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well. Wrong is worse than long.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm aware of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey, the Chamber has some concerns as well. You referred to other testimony. Of course, the summary is just about what is found in the statement, and, of course, the statement says something about the main task being translating. Now, whether you agree with that, that's of course a matter for cross-examination to challenge that and to test that evidence. But in itself, summarising that the witness in his statement says that it was his main task seems to be not inaccurate.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I believe he said as he started out that was his main task but that as his job became more involved, it was much more involved, and he wouldn't be called here as a translator merely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So this is misleading in my view.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Let's -- at least the witness said somewhere it was his main task. That's where you interrupted, I think, as a matter of fact. We do not know what Mr. Lukic would then --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I was instructed to summarise -- by Your Honours the last time to summarise the statement, and if I want to go further, I have to go further viva voce with this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In paragraph 4 of his -- of his statement --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Paragraph 4, that is what I referred to as the --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It says that his main -- "my job was mainly to translate English language materials," so that's why --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] -- put in my summary statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's what -- yes, apologies. That was what I was referring to. And that was also where I said to Mr. McCloskey that whatever the witness may have testified about in other cases, that that's, of course, not part of your summary. The summary is exclusively about this statement. Let's continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I will continue with the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: With the summary, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: He will testify about his work as an interpreter with the department in charge of maintaining relations with foreign military missions and units at the VRS Main Staff from 1994 to the end of the war, about the procedure of announcing convoys at the level of the VRS Main Staff. He will also comment on the documents related to these issues. And that would be the short statement summary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. If you'd just give me one second, Mr. Lukic. Yes, Mr. Lukic -- let me just have a look. One second, please. Please proceed. I was just checking all the redactions of the previous one because when you filed your 92 ter statement, then the redacted portions in the original were not yet redacted in the English translation, which, of course, was very confusing for us. And I was just checking that, finally, the translation, as it is uploaded, now reflects the -- at least the redaction which I found at the end of the statement. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I will start with the documents. So first I would call the document 1D2209.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Kralj, this is a document issued by the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska on the 1st of August, 1993. Let me first ask you: Where were you at the time?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KRALJ
utterances.text: At that time, I was in the 1st Krajina Corps. I was the liaison officer in the Department for Civilian Affairs, in the corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What about your corps? Did your corps receive this document? And how can we tell from this document?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KRALJ
utterances.text: Our corps received this document, indeed. You can see that in the heading where it says: "To the command of the 1st KK," standing for Krajina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In the first paragraph of this document, it says: "Following an agreement ... between the commanders of the conflicting parties in the territory of the former BH, dated the 30th of July, 1993, Article II, Rome, and the decision by the Republika Srpska government, I hereby issue the following order." This document lists what needs to be done in order for the convoy to go through. Do you remember, at the time when you were a member of the 1st Krajina Corps, whether this order was carried out and whether its stipulations were implemented?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KRALJ
utterances.text: This document based on which the command of the 1st Krajina Corps drafted its own document and implemented this order in practice, and this order is relative to the announcement of the convoy carrying humanitarian aid. Information -- and this is information to the check-points, and it also explains the procedure that needs to be complied with -- complied with in the corps, at levels ranging from the corps command down to the check-point which would be in charge of controlling the convoy.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Under 1, there is an announcement of the convoy and it says that: "Representatives of the humanitarian organisations shall give timely notifications on convoys to the Ministry of Defence of the Republika Srpska government." Did you know at the time that convoys were to be announced and were indeed announced through a civilian body; the Ministry of Defence, that is?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KRALJ
utterances.text: There were earlier attempts to announce convoys directly to the Main Staff. This order, however, regulates the matter in the following way. Convoys had to be announced to the Ministry of Defence of the government of Republika Srpska. And this was, indeed, implemented. All those who addressed the staff would be referred to the Ministry of Defence of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In paragraph 4, it says that the control of convoys carrying humanitarian aid takes place only once as the convoys enter the territory of Republika Srpska. What was the idea behind this?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KRALJ
utterances.text: The idea behind this was to avoid unnecessary delays in the passage of convoys because there were several check-points along the convoy route. Therefore, only at the entry into the territory of Republika Srpska there's control at that check-point, and the other check-points were not allowed to carry out their own controls. That resulted in the speed and enhanced security of the passage of those convoys. Also, the convoys were given escorts by the military police of the Army of Republika Srpska as well as the civilian police.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And now I would like to call up 5, where it says what the officer in charge of a convoy has to have, or has to submit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey, the fact that you are down again means that there is no intervention?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I misunderstood. I thought he was calling out a new number but I see he's referring to the paragraph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yeah. Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Are we on the right page in English, Mr. Lukic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, we are. It says crossed number 5, crossed out 5, handwritten 4.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, now are we in paragraph 5 as handwritten or as typewritten crossed out?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: 5 typewritten crossed out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So that's paragraph 4, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It says here the officer in charge of the convoy has to have an approval by the Ministry of Defence, a list of convoy personnel and their functions, a list of the convoy's escorts, a list of motor vehicles, a declaration of the type and quantities of cargo, a list of radio sets and all other technical devices mobile or integrated into the vehicle. Was this implemented in practice? Was this, indeed, requested from convoy officers? And do you know if convoy officers were aware of those obligations?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KRALJ
utterances.text: This was the first thing that was requested from the convoy officer. First he had to have an approval from the Ministry of Defence and then he had to have a list of personnel and everything else listed in here which allowed us to carry out the necessary controls. Without -- without those prerequisites, we could not carry out any controls, if those documents were missing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, are you repeating, more or less, what was read to you as the content of paragraph 4. But the question was whether this was implemented in practice.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, this was implemented in practice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The second part of this -- the third part of this composite question was: Do you know whether convoy officers were aware of those obligations? And I take it, Mr. Lukic, you refer to convoy officers from the -- accompanying the convoy and -- or did you refer to the Republika Srpska officers?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It says here the convoy officer of the humanitarian organisation. Perhaps it would be better for the witness to say how he understands this wording.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Were those officers of the VRS --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We're not going to ask the witness how he should interpret your question. Apparently you wanted to refer to convoy officers, that is Republika Srpska officers or --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Humanitarian --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Were the convoy officers that is to be understood as officers which were involved in this convoy from the humanitarian organisations, were they aware of these rules? Those who had to comply with them.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We called them convoy leaders, officers in charge of convoys. And they knew exactly what they had to have, what documents, and what to do, because they had been provided with that information from the Ministry of Defence. In other words, every convoy leader knew exactly what documents he had to have in order to be able to drive or take the -- the route that he wanted to take with the convoy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. Could I request that we be made clear in the questions that are asked whether or not this witness is speaking as the liaison officer of the 1st Krajina Corps during the time-period that he was the liaison officer of the 1st Krajina Corps, or is he speaking from his perspective as the -- his position in the Main Staff where he was part of the unit? Because it's unclear from the questions and it's certainly unclear from his answers, and it makes the world of difference. And this document is 1993. And I think -- it's clear from his summary that he wasn't a Main Staff officer at that point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, could you always clearly make a distinction between the witness talking about what he experienced as liaison officer in the 1st Krajina Corps and what he experienced in his position in the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'll do my best, Your Honour, but I think that I started my line of questions with asking this witness what was his position at this period of time in 1993. But I can clarify with him what he thinks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, if it is --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And as you know, all our discussions could be well understood by Mr. Kralj since he speaks English well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Although he has his earphones on and is most likely listening to the B/C/S version. So whether he followed our discussions is uncertain yet. But certainly this document deals with the situation, 1st of August, 1993, and onwards. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Kralj, you heard what Mr. McCloskey is concerned about. You told us that this document was, indeed, sent to your corps. You also told us that it was implemented. Were you personally aware of the contents of this document in your position at the 1st Krajina Corps?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KRALJ
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm speaking about this document from my position as the liaison officer. Because the practical implementation of this order with regard to the convoys went through me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's clear. Next question, please, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, we would tender this document into evidence now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Can we see whose name it came out in -- on to?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Maybe I should do that as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we see the last page of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Kralj, you see that at the end of this document it says "Manojlo Milovanovic." Was it customary for General Milovanovic to sign this type of documents?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KRALJ
utterances.text: Major-General Manojlo Milovanovic was a member of the Main Staff who most commonly sent out this type of documents and also signed them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. You tendered it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, no objections since we have now looked at the last page. Mr. Registrar, the document would receive number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D713, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D713 is admitted into evidence. We're not going to send it back for translation where the signature is in English "Milanovic" and not "Milovanovic." These are details, I would say. And the whole question about signatures, Mr. Lukic, this typically seems to be a telex-type of -- a telex-communicated kind of order, which it's difficult to sign them because telex machines do not accept signatures.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But still we can see some signature so that's why I said "signed." I don't know if [overlapping speakers] --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but I have got no idea whose signatures these are. The witness has not told us.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I can ask him if you want.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, if you think the witness would know, then...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kralj, can you see the signature? Are you familiar with General Milovanovic's signature? Can you recognise the signature in this document?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO KRALJ
utterances.text: It's hardly legible. It's hard to tell that this is Milovanovic's signature. And since the document was sent via an encrypted communication line, I really can't claim with certainty that this is his signature.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic, of course, it reminds me of the fact that the document bears a stamp of reception. Now, of course, I cannot exclude anything, but whether General Milovanovic would have travelled to the place where the document was received and then to sign it, that's -- well, everything is possible but it's not the most logical thing to expect, I would say. Let's leave it to that. The document is admitted. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I would call the next document, 1D2210.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And for the previous document, Mr. Lukic, I take it that you are aware that there are a lot of handwritten strike-throughs, et cetera, so what to think about this document or not, we'd like to hear from you at any point in time.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: From the position of this witness, since that document came from the Main Staff, I didn't want to enter into that debate with him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, no, I'm not saying -- but, of course, the Chamber, if interpreting such a document has a type-written text and has a lot of handwritten changes to it and then, of course, might be interested to have an answer to the question who changed it, when, before it was sent, after it was sent, when it was received, what the meaning of those changes is, I just draw your attention to those questions that are still open. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I just -- I only can say that we found it as it is so ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm not blaming you for having this version.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Paragraph 15 of your statement, Mr. Kralj, you say there that check-points were open 24 hours a day during a certain period of time. We have a document before us dated the 30th of August, 1993. We cannot see it on the screen right now, but at the bottom of the page, we have the signature of General Manojlo Milovanovic. Type-signed. Right? It's a telex. Paragraph 1 says: "Check-points must function continuously, 24 hours a day ..." Were there any problems with this kind of work?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Again, could we get a time-frame?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think that I said it's the 30th of August, 1993, when the documents -- document emanates from.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, do you mean were there any problems before or were there any problems in the implementation of the -- the question is not --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In the implementation of this 24-hour schedule.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The question now is whether there are any problems in the implementation of the 24-hour around-the-clock manning of the check-points.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] First of all, may I say that on the basis of this order it was established that check-points could operate 24 hours a day. However, after a few days, it was ascertained that that was a major problem for the passage of convoys because they move at night. And the following thing happened. Some were asking to move specifically at night-time, so the idea was to have as many convoys pass as possible. Nevertheless, when these problems appeared, UNPROFOR and other humanitarian organisation convoys, after a while, an order followed to restore things to the way they were beforehand so that there would be safety and security for all convoys.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, I'm looking at the clock.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Have you done with the document? Do you want to tendered it? Because then we might --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I would like to tender this document, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, no objections. Mr. Registrar, the number would be?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D714, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D714 is admitted into evidence. Mr. Kralj, we'll adjourn for the day. We'd like to see you back tomorrow morning at 9.30 in this same courtroom. But before you leave this courtroom, I instruct you that you should not speak or communicate in whatever way with whomever about your testimony, testimony given today or testimony still to be given, no communication whatsoever. If this is clear to you, you may follow the usher, and we'd like to see you back tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All is clear. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We adjourn for the day, and we'll resume tomorrow, Tuesday, the 28th of October, 9.30 in the morning, in this same courtroom, I.
